title: Deployments, Configuration and Self-Healing Workloads

header.html: Understand application deployments and how to perform rolling updates and rollbacks; Use ConfigMaps and Secrets to configure applications; Understand the primitives used to create robust, self-healing, application deployments

toc.title: Which workload object for which job

html:
1Which workload object for which job

Object Use it for Pod names Key facts
Deployment stateless apps random suffix owns ReplicaSets; rolling updates and rollbacks
StatefulSet apps that need stable identity or storage name-0, name-1, ... needs a governing (usually headless) Service; ordered start
DaemonSet one Pod per node (agents, log shippers) random suffix ignores replicas; needs tolerations for tainted nodes
Job run to completion random suffix completions, parallelism, restartPolicy must be Never or OnFailure
CronJob Jobs on a schedule Job per run cron schedule; suspend pauses it

Create fast: k create deployment api --image=nginx:alpine --replicas=3, k create job, k create cronjob tick --image=busybox --schedule="*/10 * * * *" -- date. A DaemonSet and a StatefulSet have no create command: generate a Deployment with --dry-run=client -o yaml and edit kind and fields.

2Rolling updates and rollbacks

A Deployment replaces Pods gradually. strategy.rollingUpdate has two knobs, each a number or a percentage:

Field Meaning Default
maxSurge how many extra Pods may exist during the update 25% (rounded up)
maxUnavailable how many Pods may be missing 25% (rounded down)

maxUnavailable: 0 with maxSurge: 2 means "never lose capacity, add two new Pods first" (Lab 5.2). strategy.type: Recreate stops all old Pods first (downtime).

k set image deployment/web nginx=nginx:stable-alpine     # container-name=image
k rollout status deployment/web                          # waits; non-zero exit if it fails
k rollout history deployment/web                         # revisions
k rollout undo deployment/web                            # previous revision
k rollout undo deployment/web --to-revision=2
k rollout pause|resume deployment/web
k scale deployment/web --replicas=5
  • k create deployment names the container after the image (nginx). k set image needs that container name: read it with k get deploy web -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[*].name}'.
  • A bad image keeps the old Pods running (with maxUnavailable: 0 rounding on 3 replicas) while new Pods show ErrImagePull or ImagePullBackOff. The update is stuck, not failed. rollout undo fixes it (Lab 5.1).
  • Only changes to the Pod template (image, env, probes) create a new revision. Scaling does not.

3ConfigMaps

A ConfigMap holds non-secret settings as key/value pairs. Three ways to create:

k create configmap app-config --from-literal=LOG_LEVEL=debug --from-literal=color=blue
k create configmap app-config --from-file=app.properties        # key = file name
k create configmap app-config --from-env-file=app.env

Three ways to use:

env:
- name: LOG_LEVEL
  valueFrom:
    configMapKeyRef: {name: app-config, key: LOG_LEVEL}   # one key as a variable
envFrom:
- configMapRef: {name: app-config}                        # every key becomes a variable
volumes:
- name: conf
  configMap: {name: app-config}                           # every key becomes a file
# plus under the container: volumeMounts: [{name: conf, mountPath: /etc/app}]
  • Mounted ConfigMaps update inside the Pod after a short delay; environment variables do not update until the Pod restarts.
  • Read the task for "from the ConfigMap, not hard-coded": a hard-coded value fails the check.

4Secrets

A Secret is like a ConfigMap for sensitive data. Values are base64 encoded, not encrypted (anyone who can read the Secret can decode it).

k create secret generic db-creds --from-literal=username=admin --from-literal=password='S3cret!'
k get secret db-creds -o jsonpath='{.data.password}' | base64 -d
k create secret docker-registry regcred --docker-server=... --docker-username=... --docker-password=...
k create secret tls web-tls --cert=tls.crt --key=tls.key

Use as env with secretKeyRef or as a volume secret: {secretName: db-creds}. Mount with readOnly: true when the task says so (Lab 5.4). Quote values with ! in the shell with single quotes.

5Self-healing primitives

Primitive What it does
ReplicaSet (via Deployment) keeps the desired number of Pods; replaces deleted or failed ones
restartPolicy (Always, OnFailure, Never) the kubelet restarts failed containers (Always is the Pod default; Jobs need the other two)
Liveness probe if it fails, the kubelet restarts the container
Readiness probe if it fails, the Pod is removed from Service endpoints (not restarted)
Startup probe holds off liveness and readiness checks for slow starters
PodDisruptionBudget (PDB) limits voluntary disruptions (node drains, evictions): minAvailable or maxUnavailable for the Pods its selector matches; k create poddisruptionbudget web-pdb --selector=app=web --max-unavailable=1; k drain waits instead of evicting a Pod that would break the budget (Lab 5.10)
Resource requests/limits scheduling and protection (Module 6)

Probe types: httpGet (path and port), tcpSocket, exec (command), grpc. Common settings: initialDelaySeconds, periodSeconds, timeoutSeconds, failureThreshold.

readinessProbe:
  httpGet: {path: /, port: 80}
  initialDelaySeconds: 3
  periodSeconds: 5
livenessProbe:
  httpGet: {path: /, port: 80}
  initialDelaySeconds: 10
  periodSeconds: 10

Break-and-fix pattern (Lab 5.9): a liveness probe pointing at the wrong port makes the container restart in a loop (RESTARTS climbs; k describe pod shows "Liveness probe failed"). A readiness probe on the wrong port leaves the Pod Running but 0/1 Ready forever. Different symptoms, same fix: correct the probe and let the rollout replace the Pods.

6StatefulSets in short

A StatefulSet gives Pods stable names (db-0, db-1) and, with a headless Service (clusterIP: None) named in serviceName, stable DNS: db-0.db.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local (Lab 5.6). Pods start in order and stop in reverse. Storage (volumeClaimTemplates) is covered in Module 10.

7Jobs and CronJobs in short

completions is how many successful Pods are needed, parallelism how many run at once, backoffLimit how many retries before failing. The Pod template must have restartPolicy: Never or OnFailure. A CronJob's schedule is five fields (minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week); */10 * * * * is every ten minutes.

8Lab tasks

<!-- LABS: m05 -->

Lab 5.1: rollback stuck update

Domain: Workloads | Points: 6 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m05-01-rollback-stuck-update)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace roll, the Deployment web (3 replicas) was updated to an image tag that does not exist, and the update is stuck. Roll the Deployment back to the previous working revision and make sure all 3 replicas are Ready.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n roll rollout history deployment web
kubectl -n roll rollout undo deployment web
kubectl -n roll rollout status deployment web --timeout=120s

Lab 5.2: rolling update strategy

Domain: Workloads | Points: 6 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m05-02-rolling-update-strategy)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace strat, the Deployment api runs 4 replicas of nginx:alpine. Change its rolling update settings to maxSurge: 2 and maxUnavailable: 0, then update the image to nginx:stable-alpine and wait for the rollout to finish.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n strat patch deployment api -p '{"spec":{"strategy":{"rollingUpdate":{"maxSurge":2,"maxUnavailable":0}}}}'
kubectl -n strat set image deployment api nginx=nginx:stable-alpine
kubectl -n strat rollout status deployment api --timeout=120s

Lab 5.3: configmap env volume

Domain: Workloads | Points: 6 | Time: about 7 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m05-03-configmap-env-volume)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace cfg, create a ConfigMap app-config with the keys LOG_LEVEL=debug and color=blue. Create a Pod cfgpod (image busybox:1.36, command sleep 3600) that:

  • gets the environment variable LOG_LEVEL from the ConfigMap key of the same name (not a hard-coded value), and
  • mounts the whole ConfigMap as files in the directory /etc/app.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n cfg create configmap app-config --from-literal=LOG_LEVEL=debug --from-literal=color=blue
kubectl -n cfg apply -f - <<Y
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: {name: cfgpod}
spec:
  containers:
  - name: main
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep", "3600"]
    env:
    - name: LOG_LEVEL
      valueFrom:
        configMapKeyRef: {name: app-config, key: LOG_LEVEL}
    volumeMounts:
    - {name: conf, mountPath: /etc/app}
  volumes:
  - name: conf
    configMap: {name: app-config}
Y
kubectl -n cfg wait --for=condition=Ready pod/cfgpod --timeout=120s
kubectl -n cfg exec cfgpod -- sh -c 'echo $LOG_LEVEL; cat /etc/app/color'

Lab 5.4: secret env file

Domain: Workloads | Points: 6 | Time: about 7 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m05-04-secret-env-file)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace sec, create a Secret db-creds with username=admin and password=S3cret!. Create a Pod dbclient (image busybox:1.36, command sleep 3600) that gets the environment variable DB_PASS from the key password of the Secret, and mounts the Secret read-only at /etc/db.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n sec create secret generic db-creds --from-literal=username=admin --from-literal=password='S3cret!'
kubectl -n sec apply -f - <<Y
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: {name: dbclient}
spec:
  containers:
  - name: main
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep", "3600"]
    env:
    - name: DB_PASS
      valueFrom:
        secretKeyRef: {name: db-creds, key: password}
    volumeMounts:
    - {name: creds, mountPath: /etc/db, readOnly: true}
  volumes:
  - name: creds
    secret: {secretName: db-creds}
Y
kubectl -n sec wait --for=condition=Ready pod/dbclient --timeout=120s

Lab 5.5: daemonset

Domain: Workloads | Points: 6 | Time: about 7 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m05-05-daemonset)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace agents, create a DaemonSet logger (image busybox:1.36, command sleep 3600) that runs one Pod on every node, including the control plane node (which has a taint).

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n agents apply -f - <<Y
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata: {name: logger}
spec:
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: logger}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: logger}}
    spec:
      tolerations:
      - {key: node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane, operator: Exists, effect: NoSchedule}
      containers:
      - {name: main, image: "busybox:1.36", command: ["sleep", "3600"]}
Y
kubectl -n agents rollout status daemonset logger --timeout=120s
kubectl -n agents get pods -o wide

Lab 5.6: statefulset

Domain: Workloads | Points: 7 | Time: about 8 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m05-06-statefulset)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace data, create a headless Service db (port 80) and a StatefulSet db with 2 replicas of nginx:alpine that uses this Service as its governing service. The Pods must be named db-0 and db-1, and db-0 must be reachable by the DNS name db-0.db.data.svc.cluster.local from inside the cluster.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n data apply -f - <<Y
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: {name: db}
spec:
  clusterIP: None
  selector: {app: db}
  ports: [{port: 80}]
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata: {name: db}
spec:
  serviceName: db
  replicas: 2
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: db}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: db}}
    spec:
      containers:
      - {name: nginx, image: "nginx:alpine"}
Y
kubectl -n data rollout status statefulset db --timeout=120s
kubectl -n data run dnstest --image=busybox:1.36 --restart=Never --rm -i -- nslookup db-0.db.data.svc.cluster.local

Lab 5.7: job cronjob

Domain: Workloads | Points: 6 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m05-07-job-cronjob)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace batch, create a Job report (image busybox:1.36, command echo done) that must complete 3 times, running 2 Pods in parallel. Also create a CronJob tick (image busybox:1.36, command date) that runs every 10 minutes.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n batch apply -f - <<Y
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata: {name: report}
spec:
  completions: 3
  parallelism: 2
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      containers:
      - {name: main, image: "busybox:1.36", command: ["echo", "done"]}
Y
kubectl -n batch create cronjob tick --image=busybox:1.36 --schedule="*/10 * * * *" -- date
kubectl -n batch wait --for=condition=Complete job/report --timeout=120s

Lab 5.8: add probes

Domain: Workloads | Points: 6 | Time: about 7 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m05-08-add-probes)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace probes, the Deployment site (2 replicas, nginx:alpine) has no health checks. Add to its container:

  • a readiness probe: HTTP GET / on port 80, initialDelaySeconds 3, periodSeconds 5;
  • a liveness probe: HTTP GET / on port 80, initialDelaySeconds 10, periodSeconds 10. All replicas must be Ready afterwards.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n probes patch deployment site -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"nginx","readinessProbe":{"httpGet":{"path":"/","port":80},"initialDelaySeconds":3,"periodSeconds":5},"livenessProbe":{"httpGet":{"path":"/","port":80},"initialDelaySeconds":10,"periodSeconds":10}}]}}}}'
kubectl -n probes rollout status deployment site --timeout=120s

Lab 5.9: fix liveness

Domain: Troubleshooting | Points: 7 | Time: about 7 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m05-09-fix-liveness)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace flaky, the Pods of the Deployment app (2 replicas, nginx:alpine) restart again and again. Find out why and fix the Deployment so that both replicas are Ready and stay running (restart count 0 on the new Pods). Do not remove the liveness probe.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n flaky describe pod -l app=app | grep -i -A2 "liveness probe failed" | head -5
kubectl -n flaky patch deployment app --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/livenessProbe/httpGet/port","value":80}]'
kubectl -n flaky rollout status deployment app --timeout=120s

Lab 5.10: pod disruption budget

Domain: Workloads | Points: 6 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m05-10-pod-disruption-budget)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace pdb, the Deployment web (3 replicas, label app=web) exists. Protect it during voluntary disruptions such as node drains: create a PodDisruptionBudget named web-pdb that selects the Pods with app=web and allows at most 1 of them to be unavailable at a time.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n pdb create poddisruptionbudget web-pdb --selector=app=web --max-unavailable=1
sleep 4
kubectl -n pdb get pdb web-pdb

<!-- /LABS -->

9Recall questions

R1Which command undoes the last rollout?

Show the answer

kubectl rollout undo deployment/<name>.

R2What do maxSurge and maxUnavailable control?

Show the answer

The extra Pods allowed and the Pods allowed to be missing during a rolling update.

R3What happens when a failed liveness probe is detected? And a failed readiness probe?

Show the answer

Liveness: the container is restarted. Readiness: the Pod stops receiving Service traffic.

R4Are Secret values encrypted?

Show the answer

No, they are base64 encoded.

R5Does an environment variable from a ConfigMap change when the ConfigMap changes?

Show the answer

No; only after the Pod restarts. Mounted files do update.

R6Why does a DaemonSet not appear on the control plane node by default?

Show the answer

The node has a NoSchedule taint; add a matching toleration.

R7Which Service type does a StatefulSet's serviceName normally point to?

Show the answer

A headless Service (clusterIP: None).

R8Which restartPolicy values are allowed in a Job's Pod template?

Show the answer

Never or OnFailure.

Quick Reference Card

Topic Remember
Update set image, rollout status/history/undo, maxSurge/maxUnavailable
Stuck rollout old Pods stay; new Pods ErrImagePull; fix with rollout undo
ConfigMap use env.valueFrom.configMapKeyRef, envFrom, volume (files)
Secret base64, secretKeyRef, volume with readOnly: true
Probes liveness restarts; readiness removes from endpoints; startup delays both
DaemonSet tolerate the control plane taint to reach all nodes
StatefulSet name-0, headless Service, stable DNS
Job completions, parallelism, restartPolicy Never/OnFailure
